docs.title: Core interfaces
docs.text:
• multids.interfaces.Readable provides read_stream(...) and read_bytes(...).
  • multids.interfaces.Writable provides write_stream(stream, ...) and write_bytes(data, ...).
  • multids.interfaces.Connector provides lifecycle methods: close() and ping().

docs.title: Workflows
docs.text:
• multids.workflows.copy_stream streams bytes between a readable and a writable connector.
  • map_records, filter_records, and batch_records compose record sources with bounded concurrency.
  • copy_records submits batches to a destination-specific bulk writer and returns a summary.

docs.title: Typed contracts
docs.text:
• ObjectRef, ObjectInfo, and ObjectPage provide portable object metadata and cursor pagination.
  • AsyncObjectStorage / SyncObjectStorage define read_object, write_object, list_object_page, and delete_object_ref.
  • AsyncRecordReader / AsyncRecordWriter and synchronous equivalents define stream_records and write_records.
  • WriteResult and BulkWriteResult report successful items, bytes, failed items, and checkpoint/continuation values.

All built-in connectors support async with or with as appropriate. Their close() methods are idempotent.

docs.title: Common connector methods
docs.text:
Connector Key methods LocalConnector read_stream(path), write_stream(stream, path), read_bytes(path), write_bytes(data, path) S3Connector read_stream(bucket, key), write_stream(stream, bucket, key, ...), write_bytes(data, bucket, key) OpenSearchConnector bulk_index(index, docs, chunk_size=500), search(index, query), scroll(index, query, scroll="1m") MySQLConnector fetch_rows(query), execute(statement), bulk_insert(table, rows, chunk_size=1000)

SQLConnectorBase (async) and SyncSQLConnectorBase implement the record-reader/record-writer contracts through stream_records, write_records, and bulk_insert; execute and execute_statement return a WriteResult whose items_written reflects the affected-row count. MySQLConnector / SyncMySQLConnector inherit this behaviour.

docs.title: AI integration
docs.text: multids.ai.AIClientInterface is a pluggable asynchronous text-generation protocol. multids.ai.OpenAIClient adapts an OpenAI-compatible async client.

docs.title: Reliability and Observability
docs.text:
Every remote connector (s3, sql, mssql, athena, opensearch, and their synchronous counterparts) shares one operational model:

  • the same retry/backoff policy for safe transient operations;
  • the same backend-exception to multids.errors mapping;
  • the same structured start / completion / retry / failure events.

docs.title: Retries and timeouts
docs.text:
Each connector accepts max_retries, backoff_factor, max_backoff and (where meaningful) timeout. These build a multids.reliability.RetryConfig.

  • Read and statement operations are retried with exponential backoff on transient failures (connection errors, server 5xx, timeouts).
  • Non-idempotent writes (bulk_insert, write_records, execute_many) are bounded by a timeout but not retried, so a retry cannot duplicate rows.
  • Cancellation (asyncio.CancelledError) always propagates immediately.
from multids.connectors.sql import MySQLConnector

conn = MySQLConnector(
    "mysql+asyncmy://user:pass@host/db",
    max_retries=5,
    backoff_factor=0.5,
    max_backoff=30.0,
    timeout=30.0,
)

docs.title: Error hierarchy
docs.text:
Backend exceptions are normalized so callers never import a driver SDK:

from multids.errors import (
    ConnectorDependencyError,   # optional dependency missing
    ConnectorConnectionError,   # unreachable backend / timeout
    ConnectorSchemaError,       # invalid statement or schema
    ConnectorDataError,         # data-level rejection
    ConnectorOperationError,    # anything else
)

from multids.connectors.s3 import S3Connector

try:
    await S3Connector().read_bytes("bucket", "missing")
except ConnectorOperationError as exc:
    ...  # 404 / rejected request
except ConnectorConnectionError as exc:
    ...  # retry or surface a connectivity problem

multids.error_mapping holds the per-backend mappers (map_sqlalchemy_error, map_botocore_error, map_pyodbc_error). A multids.errors.ConnectorError raised by a connector is passed through unchanged.

docs.title: Structured telemetry
docs.text:
Connectors emit structured events through the standard logging module at DEBUG level on the multids.connectors logger. Each event carries:

field meaning event start, completion, retry or failure backend s3, sql, mssql, athena, opensearch operation dotted operation name, e.g. sql.execute duration_seconds elapsed time for completion/failure events resource optional safe identifier (bucket/key, table) retry_number retry attempt for retry events error_type exception class name for retry/failure events

docs.title: Redaction guarantee
docs.text: TelemetryEvent has a closed set of fields. There is no payload, no SQL text, no query parameters and no credentials. resource is an operator-chosen safe identifier; never pass a secret as resource. This is why credentials, SQL parameters and record payloads cannot appear in telemetry.

docs.title: Optional tracing and metrics
docs.text:
Pass tracer and/or metrics callbacks to multids.telemetry.Telemetry and inject it into any connector. No observability provider is required.

import logging
from multids.telemetry import Telemetry, TelemetryEvent
from multids.connectors.s3 import S3Connector

logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG)

def tracer(event: TelemetryEvent) -> None:
    ...  # forward to your tracing backend

def metrics(event: TelemetryEvent) -> None:
    ...  # increment counters / histograms

telemetry = Telemetry(tracer=tracer, metrics=metrics)
conn = S3Connector(telemetry=telemetry)

Callbacks are isolated: an exception raised by a callback is logged and swallowed, so telemetry can never break data movement. Every connector exposes a telemetry attribute (a default Telemetry() when none is supplied), so the same instrumentation works uniformly across backends.

docs.title: Phase 2 design: retry safety and idempotency contract
docs.text:
Status: implemented. The contract below is realised by multids.reliability (timeout + retry), per-connector retry/timeout wiring, S3 multipart abort/resume, and workflow checkpoint callbacks. Deterministic tests live in tests/test_phase2_reliability.py.

This document is the design contract for Phase 2 (failure-safe data movement). It defines, per operation class, which failures are retryable, which operations are idempotent, and what state a caller can rely on after a failure. Implementing Phase 2 means making the connectors and workflows honour this contract and adding deterministic tests for each row.

docs.title: 1. Error classification (retry safety)
docs.text:
Retry decisions use the stable error hierarchy in multids.errors plus the raw backend exception type.

Condition Retry? Rationale asyncio.CancelledError Never Caller-initiated cancellation must propagate immediately. ConnectorDependencyError Never Missing driver/credentials will not fix itself; fail fast. ConnectorConnectionError Yes Transient network/endpoint failures (already retried by retry_async). ConnectorOperationError (base) No The backend rejected a valid request; retrying the same input fails again. ConnectorSchemaError No The request/result shape is wrong; retrying cannot help. ConnectorDataError No A specific row/document was rejected; retry needs a corrected payload, not the same one. Backend-specific transient signals (e.g. throttling, 5xx, timeouts) Yes Only when the connector maps them to ConnectorConnectionError (see Phase 3). Unknown Exception No Default to fail-safe: do not retry what we cannot classify.

Rule: a connector must only raise ConnectorConnectionError for failures that are safe to retry with the same input. Everything else must surface as a non-retryable ConnectorError (or a documented backend exception).

docs.title: 2. Idempotency classification (per operation)
docs.text:
Idempotency determines whether a workflow may safely replay an operation after a partial failure.

Operation Idempotent? Notes read_stream / read_bytes / fetch_rows Yes Reads have no side effects; safe to retry/replay. write_bytes / write_stream (no resume) Yes (last-write-wins) Re-writing the same bytes to the same key/row yields the same end state. A partial write is overwritten on retry. write_stream with resume=True (S3) Yes, via checkpoint Resumes from the last committed part; duplicate parts are de-duplicated by PartNumber + ETag. delete_object / delete_object_ref Yes (with missing_ok) Deleting an absent object is a no-op when missing_ok=True. write_object / write_json Yes (last-write-wins) Same key/bytes ⇒ same result. execute (INSERT) No Re-running inserts duplicate rows unless the table has a unique constraint / upsert. execute (UPDATE/DELETE) Conditionally Idempotent if the predicate is stable and the new value is absolute (not relative). execute_statement (DDL) Conditionally CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS is idempotent; bare CREATE TABLE is not. bulk_insert / write_records No Replaying the same batch duplicates rows. Requires an upsert or dedup key. bulk_index (OpenSearch) Yes, if id is set Same _id overwrites; without _id it duplicates. Athena query execution Yes Queries are read-only; re-running is safe (cost aside).

Rule: workflows must document which idempotency class their destination falls into, and copy_records / copy_stream must state that callers are responsible for idempotent destinations or explicit checkpoints when retries are required.

docs.title: 3. Failure-state guarantees (what a caller can rely on)
docs.text: After any operation raises, the connector must leave the system in one of these documented states:

docs.title: 3.1 Byte streams (copy_stream)
docs.text:
• Partial destination object: the destination may contain a prefix of the source bytes.
  • Resume: for S3 with resume=True, a checkpoint_path file records committed parts; a retry continues from the last committed part. Without resume, a retry restarts from byte 0 (last-write-wins).
  • No silent loss: bytes are only counted as copied after the destination writer accepts them.

docs.title: 3.2 Record batches (copy_records)
docs.text:
• At-least-once or at-most-once: batches submitted before the failure remain written (at-least-once for the successful prefix). There is no rollback of already-submitted batches.
  • No partial batch: a batch is either fully submitted or not at all (the writer is called once per batch).
  • Checkpoint: callers needing resume must pass a write_batch that is idempotent or tracks its own offset.

docs.title: 3.3 S3 multipart
docs.text: • Cleanup: on success, the multipart upload is completed and the checkpoint removed. On failure without resume, the incomplete upload is not auto-aborted (the caller/S3 lifecycle policy handles it); with resume=True, the upload id is preserved in the checkpoint for continuation.

docs.title: 3.4 SQL transactions
docs.text:
• Atomicity: execute, execute_many, bulk_insert, and write_records each run inside a single transaction (engine.begin()); a failure rolls back that transaction's writes.
  • No cross-batch atomicity: a multi-batch bulk_insert commits per batch; a mid-way failure leaves earlier batches committed.

docs.title: 3.5 OpenSearch bulk
docs.text: • Partial success: bulk_index reports per-item failures in BulkWriteResult.failed_items; successful items remain indexed. A retry re-sends only the failed items (caller's responsibility) or the whole batch (duplicates unless id is set).

docs.title: 4. Cancellation
docs.text:
• All workflow helpers (copy_stream, copy_records, map_records, filter_records, batch_records) propagate asyncio.CancelledError without swallowing it.
  • _apply_concurrently cancels in-flight tasks on any exception (including cancellation) and awaits their completion before re-raising.
  • Connectors must cancel/close in-flight network operations on cancellation (no orphaned tasks).

docs.title: 5. Test obligations (Phase 2 exit criteria)
docs.text:
For each row above, Phase 2 must add deterministic tests (mocked backends, no live services) covering:

  1. Timeout — an operation that exceeds a deadline raises ConnectorConnectionError (or documented timeout).
  2. Cancellation — cancelling a copy_stream / copy_records mid-flight stops promptly and does not leak tasks.
  3. Retry — a transient failure is retried up to max_retries, then raises; a non-retryable error is raised immediately without retry.
  4. Partial write — a failure mid-stream leaves a documented partial destination state.
  5. Replay / resume — S3 multipart resume continues from the checkpoint and does not re-upload committed parts.
  6. Rollback — a failed SQL transaction leaves no partial rows; a failed multi-batch insert leaves earlier batches.
  7. No silent loss/duplication — within the documented guarantees, records/bytes are neither lost nor duplicated.

docs.title: 6. Out of scope for Phase 2 (deferred to Phase 3)
docs.text:
• Applying retry_async uniformly to all connectors (Phase 3).
  • Mapping every backend exception to the error hierarchy (Phase 3).
  • Structured telemetry/metrics callbacks (Phase 3).

docs.title: Phase 5 — Distribution, documentation, and release controls
docs.text: Phase 5 makes installation, upgrades, and releases predictable. This page records what changed, how it is verified, and what remains before the 1.0.0 release candidate.

docs.title: Type checking
docs.text:
A [tool.mypy] configuration was added to pyproject.toml:

  • python_version = "3.11" (lowest supported interpreter)
  • files = ["src/multids"] (scope)
  • ignore_missing_imports = true (optional deps are not installed in the type-check environment)
  • check_untyped_defs = true (bodies of unannotated functions are checked)
  • no_strict_optional = true (matches runtime None-tolerance)
  • disable_error_code = ["import-untyped", "attr-defined", "assignment"] (suppresses expected noise from optional imports and dynamic attribute access)

The CI test job runs mypy src/multids after the Ruff lint step. The check must pass with zero errors.

docs.title: mypy fixes applied
docs.text: File Issue Fix connectors/mssql.py connect_pool assigned await run_operation(...) to self._pool, which mypy inferred as None from __init__ Use a local pool variable, then assign to self._pool connectors/sql.py AsyncEngine = Any fallback on ImportError # type: ignore[misc] connectors/sync/sql.py Engine = Any fallback on ImportError # type: ignore[misc] connectors/sync/sql.py text("SELECT 1") return-value annotation # type: ignore[func-returns-value] connectors/sql.py connect() did not return the awaited connection return await engine.connect()

docs.title: Ruff configuration
docs.text: The deprecated top-level [tool.ruff] select was migrated to [tool.ruff.lint] (already present in pyproject.toml). The rule set is E, F, W, C90, N.

docs.title: Dependency fix: greenlet
docs.text:
SQLAlchemy's asyncio module requires greenlet. It was listed in the mysql extra but never declared as a dependency, so pip install .[mysql] did not pull it and CI failed with:

ImportError: The SQLAlchemy asyncio module requires that the Python 'greenlet' library is installed.

Fix: greenlet = { version = ">=2.0", optional = true } added to [tool.poetry.dependencies], and greenlet added to the mysql and all extras.

docs.title: Build and artifact verification
docs.text:
python -m build          # produces dist/multids-0.2.1.tar.gz and .whl
twine check dist/*       # PASSED for all artifacts

Verified in the wheel:

  • multids/py.typed is included (PEP 561 marker).
  • greenlet appears in Requires-Dist for the mysql and all extras.
  • All extras (ai, all, local, mysql, opensearch, s3, sqlserver, sync) are declared in Provides-Extra.

docs.title: CI workflow changes
docs.text:
• ci.yml test job: added Type-check with mypy step (pip install mypy==1.8.0 && mypy src/multids).
  • real-integration.yml and benchmarks.yml: replaced the withdrawn minio/minio:latest Docker image with pgsty/silo:latest (drop-in MinIO fork; same entrypoint, env vars, and /minio/health/live endpoint).

docs.title: Remaining Phase 5 items (pre-1.0)
docs.text:
• [ ] Execute representative README and documentation examples in CI (beyond syntax-only validation).
  • [ ] Test minimal installs, each extra, wheels, and source distributions in clean virtual environments.
  • [ ] Commit a regenerated poetry.lock.
  • [ ] Publish a support matrix and compatibility policy; finalize migration / deprecation guidance.
  • [ ] Build and publish only from a protected version tag, with artifact checks, changelog verification, and dependency / security scanning (pip-audit).

docs.title: multids Quickstart
docs.text:
This quickstart shows how to install the package with common extras and run simple operations with the connectors.

Install with extras you need (example: OpenSearch + SQL Server + S3):

pip install "multids[opensearch,sqlserver,s3]"

Basic usage examples:

  • Read a local file:
import asyncio
from multids.connectors.local import LocalConnector


async def main():
    lc = LocalConnector()
    async for chunk in lc.read_stream("./data/example.txt"):
        print(chunk)


asyncio.run(main())
  • Upload bytes to S3 (single PUT or multipart depending on size):
import asyncio
from multids.connectors.s3 import S3Connector


async def upload():
    s3 = S3Connector(region_name="eu-central-1")
    await s3.write_bytes(b"small payload", "my-bucket", "path/to/key")
    await s3.close()


asyncio.run(upload())
  • Bulk index documents into OpenSearch:
import asyncio
from multids.connectors.opensearch import OpenSearchConnector


async def index():
    oc = OpenSearchConnector("http://localhost:9200")
    docs = [{"id": "1", "title": "hello"}, {"id": "2", "title": "world"}]
    await oc.bulk_index("my-index", docs)
    await oc.close()


asyncio.run(index())

See the docs/usage.md for more advanced examples (S3 multipart resume, streaming reads, SQL bulk inserts).

docs.title: Supported Python versions
docs.text: multids supports Python 3.11, 3.12, and 3.13. The project follows semantic versioning: breaking public API changes are released only in a new major version; supported APIs receive a deprecation notice for at least one minor release before removal.

docs.title: Connector support
docs.text:
Backend Async Sync Install extra Contracts Notes Local files Yes Yes local Async/SyncObjectStorage Async mode uses aiofiles. Amazon S3 Yes Yes s3 Async/SyncObjectStorage Async multipart/resume support. OpenSearch Yes No opensearch AsyncRecordReader, AsyncRecordWriter Compatible with Elasticsearch-style APIs. Athena Yes Yes s3 / sync Async/SyncRecordReader Read-only; requires AWS credentials and an output location. MySQL Yes Yes mysql / sync Async/SyncRecordReader, Async/SyncRecordWriter Uses SQLAlchemy plus asyncmy or PyMySQL. SQL Server Yes Yes sqlserver Async/SyncRecordReader, Async/SyncRecordWriter Requires an OS ODBC driver; unavailable on Python 3.12+.

Every connector conforms to the capability protocols in multids.contracts: object-storage connectors implement read_object, write_object, list_object_page, and delete_object_ref; record connectors implement stream_records and/or write_records. All connectors support async with / with as appropriate and expose idempotent close() methods. See docs/api.md for the full contract reference.

docs.title: CLI
docs.text:
The built-in CLI deliberately starts with safe local-file operations:

multids ping --path ./data
multids copy ./data/input.jsonl ./out/input.jsonl
multids validate workflow.json

validate accepts a JSON object with command set to ping or copy. Copy configurations must declare local source and destination paths. Remote CLI profiles will be added only after credential handling is designed safely.

docs.title: Integration tests and benchmarks
docs.text:
Normal CI runs deterministic unit tests (including contract-conformance tests that verify every connector against the capability protocols), documentation-example validation, and formatting/lint checks.

The Real Service Integration workflow runs a backend matrix against disposable services:

Backend Service Python versions Notes S3 MinIO (S3-compatible) 3.11–3.13 Auth, Unicode, multipart, pagination, cleanup, resume MySQL mysql:8.0 container 3.11–3.13 Unicode, pagination, large streams, failure recovery SQL Server mssql/server:2022-latest container 3.11 ODBC driver installed in CI; pyodbc is <3.12 only OpenSearch opensearchproject/opensearch:2.9.0 3.11–3.13 Bulk, scroll pagination, large loads, failure recovery Athena AWS (repository secrets) 3.11 Opt-in; skips when secrets are absent

Integration tests live in tests/integration/ and are marked real_integration. They skip cleanly when the required environment variables are not set, so they never fail a local or PR run.

docs.title: Benchmarks
docs.text:
Reproducible benchmarks for S3 transfer, SQL batch inserts and OpenSearch bulk indexing live in benchmarks/, driven by tools/benchmarks.py:

# Record results (SQL/SQLite runs offline; S3/OpenSearch run when configured)
python tools/benchmarks.py --output benchmarks/results.json

# Compare against the committed baseline and fail on material regressions
python tools/benchmarks.py --compare benchmarks/baseline.json --tolerance 0.25

benchmarks/baseline.json records the committed results. The SQL/SQLite baseline is reproducible on any machine with SQLAlchemy; the S3 and OpenSearch entries are populated by the Benchmarks workflow when those services are available. A throughput regression beyond --tolerance fails the benchmark job.

docs.title: Usage Examples
docs.text:
This document contains more detailed usage examples and patterns for the common connectors in multids.

1) S3 multipart upload with resume and progress

import asyncio

from multids.connectors.s3 import S3Connector


async def run():
    s3 = S3Connector(region_name="eu-central-1")

    # Example stream (could be an aiofiles stream, generator, or bytes)
    async def gen_bytes():
        for i in range(10):
            yield (b"x" * 1024 * 1024)  # 1MB chunks

    def progress(part_number, bytes_uploaded):
        print(f"part={part_number} bytes={bytes_uploaded}")

    await s3.write_stream(
        gen_bytes(),
        "my-bucket",
        "big-file.bin",
        checkpoint_path="./.s3-checkpoint.json",
        progress_callback=progress,
        force_multipart=True,
    )
    await s3.close()


asyncio.run(run())

The connector also handles S3 pagination for you when listing objects:

async for key in s3.list_keys("my-bucket", prefix="exports/"):
    print(key)

await s3.delete_object("my-bucket", "exports/old-file.json")

OpenSearch calls raise stable exceptions from multids.errors. Handle ConnectorConnectionError for exhausted transient retries, ConnectorDependencyError for a missing optional package, and ConnectorDataError when a bulk backend reports rejected data. OpenSearch uses exponential backoff by default; tune it with max_retries, backoff_factor, and max_backoff on OpenSearchConnector.

2) Streaming search results from OpenSearch

import asyncio
from multids.connectors.opensearch import OpenSearchConnector


async def stream_search():
    oc = OpenSearchConnector("http://localhost:9200")
    # simple scroll helper; `search` returns raw ES response
    res = await oc.search("my-index", {"query": {"match_all": {}}}, size=100)
    # use `scroll` to iterate if you need many hits
    async for hit in oc.scroll("my-index", {"query": {"match_all": {}}}):
        print(hit)
    await oc.close()


asyncio.run(stream_search())

3) MySQL bulk insert

import asyncio
from multids.connectors.sql import MySQLConnector


async def bulk_insert():
    mysql = MySQLConnector("mysql+asyncmy://user:pass@localhost:3306/db")
    rows = [{"id": i, "name": f"name-{i}"} for i in range(1000)]
    await mysql.bulk_insert("users", rows, chunk_size=200)
    await mysql.close()


asyncio.run(bulk_insert())

4) Using an OpenAI-compatible client for enrichment

from openai import AsyncOpenAI
from multids.ai import OpenAIClient
from multids.connectors.opensearch import OpenSearchConnector

ai = OpenAIClient(AsyncOpenAI())
oc = OpenSearchConnector("http://localhost:9200")


# Fetch docs, enrich text, and re-index.
async def enrich_and_index():
    docs = [{"id": "1", "text": "OpenSearch + AI"}]
    for d in docs:
        d["summary"] = (await ai.generate(d["text"], model="gpt-4o-mini"))["content"]
    await oc.bulk_index("my-index", docs)
    await oc.close()

5) Athena query streaming

import asyncio
from multids.connectors.athena import AthenaConnector


async def run_query():
    ac = AthenaConnector(region_name="eu-central-1", workgroup=None)
    async for row in ac.query_stream("SELECT * FROM sample_table", database="default"):
        print(row)


asyncio.run(run_query())

docs.title: Data movement workflows
docs.text: multids.workflows provides the small amount of orchestration needed to make connectors useful together. It does not create or close connectors; callers retain ownership of their lifecycle and credentials.

docs.title: Copy an object without buffering it
docs.text:
copy_stream passes the source byte stream straight into the destination writer. source_args and destination_args are the positional arguments each connector expects after the stream argument.

from multids.connectors.local import LocalConnector
from multids.connectors.s3 import S3Connector
from multids.workflows import copy_stream

local = LocalConnector(base_path="./exports")
s3 = S3Connector(region_name="eu-central-1")

result = await copy_stream(
    local,
    s3,
    source_args=("daily/events.jsonl",),
    destination_args=("my-bucket", "exports/events.jsonl"),
)
print(result.bytes_copied, result.chunks_copied)

The example is equally useful for S3-to-local copies; swap the connectors and arguments. The entire object is never held in memory by the workflow helper.

docs.title: Transform and batch records
docs.text:
Record helpers accept either an Iterable or an AsyncIterable. Mapping and filtering accept normal or async functions. concurrency bounds active async work and still preserves source order.

from multids.workflows import batch_records, filter_records, map_records

async def enrich(row):
    return {**row, "normalized": row["name"].strip().lower()}

rows = [{"name": "Alice"}, {"name": "Bob"}, {"name": " "}]
enriched = map_records(rows, enrich, concurrency=10)
valid = filter_records(enriched, lambda row: bool(row["normalized"]))

async def write_batch_somewhere(batch):
    ...  # forward each batch to a destination connector

async for batch in batch_records(valid, size=500):
    await write_batch_somewhere(batch)

docs.title: Practical destinations
docs.text:
Wrap a connector-specific bulk operation in a small batch writer and use copy_records to obtain a success summary.

from multids.workflows import copy_records

# Athena -> SQL
async def insert_rows(batch):
    await mysql.bulk_insert("events", batch)

summary = await copy_records(athena.query_stream("SELECT * FROM events"), insert_rows)

# SQL -> OpenSearch
async def index_rows(batch):
    await opensearch.bulk_index("events", batch)

summary = await copy_records(mysql.fetch_rows("SELECT * FROM events"), index_rows, batch_size=500)

docs.title: S3 JSONL to OpenSearch
docs.text:
import json

from multids.workflows import copy_records

async def json_lines():
    remainder = b""
    async for chunk in s3.read_stream("my-bucket", "exports/events.jsonl"):
        lines = (remainder + chunk).split(b"\n")
        remainder = lines.pop()
        for line in lines:
            if line:
                yield json.loads(line)
    if remainder:
        yield json.loads(remainder)

async def index_rows(batch):
    await opensearch.bulk_index("events", batch)

summary = await copy_records(json_lines(), index_rows, batch_size=500)

docs.title: Failures, cancellation, and checkpoints
docs.text:
The helpers propagate exceptions and asyncio.CancelledError; they do not silently retry or swallow a failed destination write. A failed stream may leave a partial destination object, while records in batches submitted before the failure remain written. Use idempotent destination writes where possible.

For resumable S3 destinations, pass checkpoint_path and resume through destination_kwargs in copy_stream. The S3 connector owns its checkpoint and multipart cleanup behavior; on failure without a checkpoint it aborts the incomplete multipart upload, and with a checkpoint it persists state so a retry resumes from the last committed part (committed parts are not re-uploaded).

Both copy_stream and copy_records accept an optional checkpoint callback that is invoked with the cumulative result after each chunk/batch. Use it to persist a resume offset for your own destination:

from multids.workflows import copy_records

async def save_offset(result):
    ...  # persist result.records_copied somewhere durable

summary = await copy_records(records, write_batch, batch_size=500, checkpoint=save_offset)

Retries and per-attempt timeouts are handled by the connectors themselves (see multids.reliability): read and statement operations are retried with exponential backoff on transient failures, while non-idempotent bulk writes (bulk_insert, write_records) are bounded by a timeout but not retried, to avoid duplicating rows.
